title: Kumamon
lede: Kumamoto Prefecture’s black bear mascot, made by art director Manabu Mizuno in 2010 for the Kyushu Shinkansen opening: round eyes, red cheek circles, and an open smile.
summary: Black round-headed bear with white eyes, red cheek circles, and a wide smile. Manabu Mizuno for Kumamoto Prefecture, 2010.

creator.name: Manabu Mizuno (Good Design Company) for Kumamoto Prefecture

evidence.note: Inspected the photograph [Kumamon on the wall](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kumamon_on_the_wall_(14987894668).jpg) by foooomio (2014, CC BY 2.0, 1280 px scratchpad copy), which shows a large Kumamon face on the glass facade of an office building in central Kumamoto. Not stored, because the character is its main subject.

styles.note: Partial fit: a yuru-chara with the kawaii face (round eyes, blush circles, big head), but drawn in black, white, and red instead of pastels.

context: Wikipedia says Kumamon was established in 2010 by the Kumamoto Prefecture government, in a campaign to draw tourists after the Kyushu Shinkansen line opened, and ranked first in the 2011 nationwide mascot competition with more than 280,000 votes. [Wikipedia: Kumamon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumamon).
Kumamoto Prefecture grants usage rights for free when products promote goods and services from the prefecture. [Wikipedia: Kumamon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumamon).

UWC ISAK Japan names Manabu Mizuno, creative director of Good Design Company, as the creator of Kumamon. [UWC ISAK Japan](https://uwcisak.jp/blog/news-events/guest-speaker-manabu-mizuno-creator-of-kumamon/).
observed: On the building, the face covers several storeys of glass: a black round head with two small round ears.
The eyes are white circles with black pupils, set high and wide; two solid red circles mark the cheeks.
A white muzzle with a wide open mouth sits low in the face.
The surrounding city street, signs, and tram tracks are ordinary; the face is the only character in view.
interpretation: Kumamon shows how the yuru-chara branch carries the kawaii face into public promotion and signage. The strong black and red make it readable at building scale, which pastels would not.
Compared with Sanrio characters, the face is more graphic and less sweet, close to a logo.
borrow: Reduce a mascot to a few flat shapes (head, two eyes, two cheek circles, a muzzle) so it reads at any size.
Keep cheek blush as two solid circles of one color.

rights.statement: No image is stored. Kumamon is © Kumamoto Prefecture and used under its licensing scheme. The Commons photograph is CC BY 2.0, but its main subject is the character.
